πειράζουσι διδόναι ἀλλὰ πιστῶς αἰτοῦσιν–, ὁ μέντοι λόγος ἐκβέβληται πάντη ὡς
ἐπιβουλεύων τῇ δόξῃ τοῦ σταυροῦ. Ἡμεῖς δὲ κηρύσσομεν Χριστὸν ἐσταυρωμένον
καὶ τὰ ἑξῆς. δηλονότι Χριστὸν θεοῦ δύναμιν καὶ θεοῦ σοφίαν κατὰ τὸν τοῦ σταυροῦ
λόγον φησίν, ὡς ἀνωτέρω· ὁ λόγος γὰρ ὁ τοῦ σταυροῦ τοῖς μὲν ἀπολλυμένοις μωρία
ἐστίν, τοῖς δὲ σωζομένοις ἡμῖν δύναμις θεοῦ ἐστιν. καὶ τὰ ἑξῆς δείκνυσι τοῦτο
τρανότερον· μετὰ γὰρ τὸ φάναι· αὐτοῖς δὲ τοῖς κλητοῖς,Ἰουδαίοις τε καὶἝλλησιν,
Χριστὸν θεοῦ δύναμιν καὶ θεοῦ σοφίαν, ἐπήγαγεν· διότι τὸ μωρὸν τοῦ θεοῦ
σοφώτερον τῶν ἀνθρώπων ἐστίν, καὶ τὸ 230 ἀσθενὲς τοῦ θεοῦ ἰσχυρότερον τῶν
ἀνθρώπων ἐστίν. τίς δ' ἂν εἴποι τὸν θεὸν λόγον τὸ ἀσθενὲς τοῦ θεοῦ εἰρῆσθαι, καὶ
μωρὸν τοῦ θεοῦ περὶ ἐσταυρωμένου Χριστοῦ τὸ λεγόμενον; θεὸς λόγος δυνατὸς ὡς ὁ
πατήρ, οὐ δύναμις μέρος συμπληρωματικὸν τῆς οὐσίας τῆς πατρικῆς, ὁμοίως καὶ
σοφός, ἐπειδὴ γὰρ ὅπερ οὐκ ἴσχυσεν ἡ ὁρωμένη κτίσις ἢ ἄγγελοι ἢ ἀρχάγγελοι
κατιόντες οὐρανόθεν, πατριάρχαι καὶ προφῆται, νόμος ὁ διὰ Μωϋσέως, φωναὶ αἱ ἐκ
μέσου τοῦ πυρὸς ἐνεχθεῖσαι πρὸς τὸν λαὸν διὰ τὸ μὴ συγχωρεῖν τὴν τῶν
ἀγνωμονούντων προαίρεσιν, τοῦτο τοῦ σταυροῦ ἡ μωρία ἴσχυσεν. διὰ τοῦτο θεοῦ
δύναμις καὶ θεοῦ σοφία Χριστὸς ἐσταυρωμένος, πάσης τῆς οἰκονομίας ἀνυτικώτερος
καὶ πάσης τῆς κτίσεως ἀξιοπιστότερος. καὶ τοῦτο δὲ δύναμις τοῦ οἰκονομήσαντος
καὶ κατορθώσαντος, ἐν τῷ μηδενὶ σώσαντος τοὺς ἀνθρώπους καὶ εἰς τὴν εἰς αὐτὸν
πίστιν ἀγαγόντος. 229,ξολ2ἘπειδὴἸουδαῖοι τοῦ θεοῦ τὸ πνεῦμα πειράζουσιν, ἀλλὰ
τοῖς πιστεύουσιν χαρίζεσθαι, οὔτε μὴνἝλλησι τῇ λογιότητι κατακοσμεῖν οἰομένοις
τὴν εὐσέβειαν ἀποκρίνασθαι δεῖ, εἶτα διδάσκει πῶς δοκεῖ εἶναι μωρία τὸ κήρυγμα·
ἐκεῖνοι μὲν γὰρ σημεῖα καὶ σοφίαν ζητοῦσιν, ἡμεῖς κηρύσσομεν Χριστὸν
ἐσταυρωμένον θεοῦ δύναμιν καὶ σοφίαν, καὶ παρὰ τοῦ ἐσταυρωμένου σωτηρίαν τοῖς
πιστεύουσιν ἐπαγγελλόμεθα. 230,ξολ2 Οὐ χρὴ τὸν θεὸν λόγον τὸ ἀσθενὲς τοῦ θεοῦ
εἰρῆσθαι, ἀλλὰ τὸν σταυρὸν τοῦ Χριστοῦ· ὁ γὰρ λόγος δυνατὸς ὡς ὁ πατήρ, οὐ
δύναμις ὡς μέρος συμπληρωτικὸν τῆς οὐσίας τοῦ πατρός. οὕτω δὲ καὶ ὁ υἱὸς σοφὸς
ὡς ὁ πατήρ. ἐπειδὴ δὲ ὃ οὐκ ἴσχυσαν ποιῆσαι ἄγγελοι, οὐ νόμος, οὐ προφῆται, διὰ τὸ
συγχωρεῖν τὸν θεὸν τῇ τῶν ἀγνωμόνων προαιρέσει, τοῦτο ἡ δοκοῦσα τοῦ σταυροῦ
μωρία ἴσχυσεν, θεοῦ δύναμις καὶ σοφία Χριστὸς ἐσταυρωμένος κηρύσσεται, ὡς
ἰσχυρότερος καὶ ἀνυστικώτερος ὠφθεὶς καὶ τοὺς πιστεύοντας σώσας. 1 Kor 1,26 Τὸ
κατὰ σάρκα προσέθηκεν ἀντιδιαστέλλων τῷ πνεύματι, καὶ τὰ ἑξῆς ὁμοίως κατὰ
κοινοῦ ἀποδιδούς. 1 Kor 1,29 Ὅπως μὴ καυχήσηται πᾶσα σὰρξ ἐνώπιον αὐτοῦ, τοῦτ'
ἔστιν ἵνα μὴ τοῖς οἰκείοις πλεονεκτήμασιν ἐπιγράψωσι τὸ κατόρθωμα τοῦ
κηρύγματος. σὰρξ δὲ εἶπεν καὶ οὐ ψυχή, ἐξευτελίζων τὰ ἀνθρώπινα καυχήματα. διὰ
τί δὲ ἐνώπιον αὐτοῦ καὶ οὐκ ἐνώπιον ἀνθρώπων; ὅτι τῇ ἐπὶ τῷ θεῷ καυχήσει
ἀντετάττετο ἡ ἐπὶ τοῖς ἡμετέροις πλεονεκτήμασι καύχησις· ἃ γὰρ ἐχρῆν ἐπιγράφειν
θεῷ, 231 ἐπέγραφον ἀνθρώποις. διὰ τοῦτο τὸ ἐνώπιον αὐτοῦ εἴρηκεν· καὶ γὰρ ἦν
ἀσεβὴς ἡ καύχησις ἐνώπιον τοῦ πάντα ὁρῶντος γινομένη. ὅτι δὲ τὸ ἐνώπιον αὐτοῦ
οὐκ ἐν τῇ παρουσίᾳ εἴρηκεν, αὕτη ἡ ὅλη ὑπόθεσις δείκνυσιν· δεῖ γὰρ τοῖς ἐπὶ λόγοις
καυχωμένοις καὶ ἐπὶ τῷ βαπτίζειν καυχᾶσθαι, καὶ ἐφ' ἑτέροις τισὶν ποιεῖται τὸν
λόγον. 1 Kor 1,30 Ἐξ αὐτοῦ δὲ ὑμεῖς ἐστε. πάντες ὁμοίως κατὰ τὸ σεσῶσθαί φασιν
εἰρῆσθαι νῦν, οὐ κατὰ τὸν τῆς δημιουργίας λόγον, ὥς φησιν ἀλλαχοῦ· οἳ οὐκ ἐξ
αἱμάτων οὐδὲ ἐκ θελήματος σαρκὸς ἀλλ' ἐκ θεοῦ ἐγεννήθησαν. εἰ τοίνυν ἐξ αὐτοῦ,
πῶς καυχησώμεθα ἐν ἰδίοις πλεονεκτήμασιν; τὸ δὲ ἐν ΧριστῷἸησοῦ, ὃς ἐγενήθη
ἡμῖν σοφία καὶ ἁγιασμὸς καὶ ἀπολύτρωσις· οὐκ ἀνθρώπων σοφία ἔσωσεν–ἐπλανᾶτο
γάρ–ἀλλ' αὐτὸς ἡμῖν σοφία γέγονεν εἰς θεογνωσίαν· οὐκ ἀνθρώπων σύνεσις
ἥρπασεν, ἀλλὰἸησοῦς σταυρωθείς. οὐκ ἄνθρωποι ἀπελυτρώσαντο, ὥστε τὸ καύχημα
ἀπὸ τοῦ σώσαντος γενέσθω, μὴ ἀπὸ τῶν σωθέντων. 1 Kor 2,3–4Ἐφοβούμην ἀεί, μὴ
τῇ ἔξωθεν παιδεύσει ἐπαρθῆτε, αὐτίκα οὐκ ἐχρησάμην τῇ πειθούσῃ σοφίᾳ. ἐν
ἀσθενείᾳ δέ, λέγει, τῇ ἀπὸ τῶν διωγμῶν–τοῦτο γὰρ πανταχοῦ ἔθος αὐτῷ λέγειν–ἐν
ἀσθενείᾳ καὶ ἐν φόβῳ καὶ ἐν τρόμῳ τὸ ἀσθενὲς ἐξ ὧν ἐδιωκόμην. ἐπεδεικνύμην τὸν
φόβον καὶ τὸν τρόμον τὸν περὶ ὑμῶν, πάντα ἤμην ταπεινός, ἵνα ὑμεῖς τούτῳ
διδαχθῆτε καὶ μὴ ἐπαίρησθε.Ἐπειδὴ εἶπεν· ὁ λόγος μου, ἵνα μὴ δόξῃ τὸ ἐναντίον
pass_a_gloss: (Continuing: for not to those who) test (are signs) to be given, but to those who ask faithfully -, the word (eloquence) however has been thrown out entirely as plotting against the glory of the cross. 'But we preach Christ crucified' and the following. Clearly he calls Christ power of God and wisdom of God according to the word of the cross, as above: 'For the word of the cross to those perishing is foolishness, but to us who are saved it is the power of God' (1 Cor 1:18). And the following (words) show this more distinctly: for after saying 'but to the called themselves, Jews and Greeks, Christ power of God and wisdom of God', he added: 'because the foolish of God is wiser than men, and the weak of God is stronger than men'. Who would say God the Word to be called 'the weak of God', and the 'foolish of God' - what is said (is) about Christ crucified? God the Word (is) powerful as the Father, not a power (as) a part completing the paternal substance; likewise also wise. For since what the seen creation was not able (to do), or angels or archangels coming down from heaven, patriarchs and prophets, the law through Moses, voices brought from the middle of the fire to the people, because the choice of the obstinate did not permit (it) - this the foolishness of the cross was able (to do). Because of this Christ crucified (is) power of God and wisdom of God, more effective than the whole dispensation and more trustworthy than the whole creation. And this also (is) power of the one who arranged and accomplished (it), in saving humans by nothing and leading (them) to faith in him. [Second column, page 229, parallel to the 1:22-24 note:] Since Jews test the Spirit of God, but (it is) to grant (signs) to those who believe, nor indeed must one answer Greeks who think to adorn godliness with learning, then he teaches how the preaching seems to be foolishness: for they seek signs and wisdom, we preach Christ crucified, power of God and wisdom, and we promise salvation from the crucified one to those who believe. [Second column, page 230, parallel to the 1:25 note:] God the Word must not be called the weak of God, but the cross of Christ; for the Word is powerful as the Father, not a power as a part completing the substance of the Father. So also the Son is wise as the Father. And since what angels were not able to do, not law, not prophets, because God gives way to the choice of the obstinate, this the seeming foolishness of the cross was able (to do), Christ crucified is preached as power of God and wisdom, as shown stronger and more effective and having saved those who believe. [Label 1 Cor 1:26.] He added 'according to flesh' setting (it) against the Spirit, and supplying (it) likewise in common to the following. [Label 1 Cor 1:29.] 'So that all flesh may not boast before him', that is, so that they may not ascribe the success of the preaching to (their) own advantages. And he said flesh and not soul, cheapening human boasts. Why 'before him' and not 'before men'? Because the boasting over our advantages was set against the boasting in God; for what they ought to ascribe to God, they ascribed to men. For this reason he has said 'before him': for the boasting was impious, happening before the one who sees all. That he did not say 'before him' in (reference to) the Coming, this whole subject shows: for it is necessary (to deal) with those boasting over words and boasting over baptizing, and he makes the discourse about certain other (matters). [Label 1 Cor 1:30.] 'But of him you are.' All alike say (it) is said now according to being saved, not according to the account of creation, as it says elsewhere: 'who were born not of bloods nor of the will of flesh but of God' (John 1:13). If then (we are) of him, how shall we boast in own advantages? And 'in Christ Jesus, who became for us wisdom and sanctification and redemption': not wisdom of men saved - for it was wandering - but he himself has become wisdom for us toward knowledge of God; not understanding of men seized (us), but Jesus crucified. Not men redeemed, so let the boast come from the one who saved, not from those saved. [Label 1 Cor 2:3-4.] I was afraid always lest you be lifted up by the outside education; so I did not use the persuading wisdom. 'And in weakness', he says, the (weakness) from the persecutions - for this is his custom to say everywhere - 'in weakness and in fear and in trembling', the weak (state) from (those by) whom I was persecuted. I displayed the fear and the trembling about you, I was lowly in all, so that you might be taught by this and not be lifted up. Since he said 'my word', so that he might not seem the opposite (… continues in the next section).
pass_b_english: …to give them to those who put God to the test, but to those who ask in faith), then eloquence is ruled out altogether, as a plot against the glory of the cross. "But we preach Christ crucified," and the rest. Plainly he calls Christ the power of God and the wisdom of God with respect to the word of the cross, as he did above: "For the word of the cross is folly to those who are perishing, but to us who are being saved it is the power of God" (1 Corinthians 1:18). What follows makes this clearer still. After saying, "but to those who are called, both Jews and Greeks, Christ the power of God and the wisdom of God," he added, "because the foolishness of God is wiser than men, and the weakness of God is stronger than men." Who would say that God the Word is what is meant by "the weakness of God"? "The foolishness of God" is said of Christ crucified. God the Word is powerful as the Father is, not a power that is a part filling out the Father's substance; and he is wise in the same way. What the visible creation could not achieve, nor angels or archangels coming down from heaven, nor patriarchs and prophets, nor the law given through Moses, nor the voices carried to the people from the midst of the fire, because the choice of the obstinate would not allow it, the foolishness of the cross achieved. That is why Christ crucified is the power of God and the wisdom of God: he accomplished more than the whole dispensation and carried more conviction than all creation. This too is the power of the one who planned it and brought it off: he saved human beings by what counts for nothing and led them to faith in himself.

The second catena form adds: Then he teaches how the preaching seems to be foolishness. They look for signs and wisdom; we preach Christ crucified, the power and wisdom of God, and we promise those who believe salvation from the one who was crucified.
On 1 Corinthians 1:26: He added "according to the flesh" to set it against the Spirit, and the phrase serves in common for the words that follow.

On 1 Corinthians 1:29: "So that no flesh may boast before him": that is, so that they may not credit the success of the preaching to their own advantages. He said "flesh" and not "soul" to belittle human boasting. Why "before him" and not "before men"? Because boasting in our own advantages had been set up against boasting in God: what they ought to have credited to God, they credited to men. That is why he said "before him," for boasting carried on in the sight of the one who sees all things was impious. The whole subject shows that he did not say "before him" with the Coming in view, for he has to deal with people who boast of eloquence and of having baptized, and he is speaking about such matters as these.

On 1 Corinthians 1:30: "But of him you are." Everyone alike says that this is said here of being saved, not in the sense of creation, as it says elsewhere: "who were born, not of blood nor of the will of the flesh, but of God" (John 1:13). If then we are of him, how can we boast in advantages of our own? Next, "in Christ Jesus, who became for us wisdom and sanctification and redemption." Human wisdom did not save us, for it was going astray; he himself became our wisdom, to bring us to know God. No human understanding snatched us away; Jesus crucified did. Men did not redeem us. So let the boast be drawn from the one who saved, not from those who were saved.

On 1 Corinthians 2:3–4: I was always afraid that outside learning would puff you up, so I did not use persuasive wisdom. "In weakness," he says, meaning the weakness that comes from persecution, for that is how he always speaks: "in weakness and in fear and in trembling," the weakness caused by those who persecuted me. I showed the fear and trembling I felt for you; I was lowly in everything, so that you might learn from this and not be puffed up. Since he had said "my speech," so that he would not seem to be putting forward the very thing opposed…

lemmas.gloss: in common (one word serving several clauses)

choices.english: collapsed; one sentence kept as 'The second catena form adds:'
choices.why: Both are second-column forms of the 1:22-25 notes already translated from the first column. Only the sentence promising salvation from the crucified one has no counterpart, so only it is printed.
rejected: printing both forms (old English, SOURCE_ISSUES item 7)

choices.term: διὰ τὸ μὴ συγχωρεῖν τὴν τῶν ἀγνωμονούντων προαίρεσιν
choices.english: because the choice of the obstinate would not allow it
choices.why: τὴν προαίρεσιν is the subject of the infinitive. The second form words it differently (God gives way to the choice of the obstinate); recorded in translator_notes, not printed.
rejected: which could not forgive the choice of the ungrateful

choices.english: not ... with the Coming in view
choices.why: παρουσία in exegesis of 'before him' means the Coming (judgement), not mere presence.

choices.term: δεῖ γὰρ τοῖς ... καυχᾶσθαι, καὶ ἐφ' ἑτέροις τισὶν ποιεῖται τὸν λόγον
choices.english: he has to deal with people who boast of eloquence and of having baptized, and he is speaking about such matters as these
choices.why: The clause is awkward in the Greek; rendered as closely as it allows without adding an argument.
